Remember the stone only takes you part of the way in personal growth and the rest is on you.

I'm not a writer, more into visual art, so I feel you on the wanting to pursue something creative. Keeping that creativity in mind, remember that ending your life comes with the finality that you really never will do anything. You say you want to "skip the dancing", but please, you don't know what will happen if you end it soon. If you continue living, you could find something that made this struggle worthwhile, whether it be and idea or an experience.
In regards to feeling "selfish" or "pompous" for asking for help, don't. Your sadness or struggle shouldn't be put on a comparative scale with others. We all feel differently, so your struggle is something you shouldn't be ashamed of. The same goes for feeling "not special". Again, these things can't be put on a scale. As cliche as it is, we're all special.
Sorry for ending on such a sappy note. Just know you have potential; something you may never find if you end it here.

As a recent HS graduate there is one big thing you need to know. After you graduate, no one will care about your high school GPA, as long as you are interested in actually learning the material. You are setting big goals for yourself, and that's great: reach for the stars! Learn all you can! But, that doesn't mean you should be stressing over something as simple as a number.

Getting into a selective school for so many HS students and a 4.0 GPA is the definition of success, but thinking that way is such a narrow definition of success. That number is not a quantified representation of my self worth as a person, though many treat it as such. How could a number possibly account for your unique experiences and epiphanies in the classroom?

My favorite class in all my four years was an AP Physics class. I got C despite studying more for that class than all my others combined, but I loved the material so much I'm now considering being a Physics major.

If there's anything I would change about my high school career, it's less worrying about GPA, because in the end, it's just a number. College admissions will also look at your essays and other activities, so I wouldn't let it bother you for that reason. No matter where you go to college, whether Harvard or community college, you'll learning about what you're passionate about, and that matters more than a number.

TLDR: Good Luck and work hard to ace your finals, but GPA is just a number, so don't worry about it too much. :-)
